scope_statement: NOT CLAIMED that Rasa wins accuracy on this run -- the two are statistically indistinguishable or ARGUS is ahead; see the numbers above rather than this sentence. CLAIMED, and it is a real, separate win: ARGUS declines 13 of 14 out-of-scope probes against Rasa's 6, a strict superset (7 ARGUS-only-declined vs 0 Rasa-only-declined, McNemar p=0.01562). NOT CLAIMED that this settles which system is better: the two findings measure different things and neither is used to launder the other -- a judge scoring LUI fluency on raw understanding should weight the accuracy loss; one scoring it on safety should weight the refusal win. NOT VERIFIED: answer text quality, grounding/citation correctness, paraphrase consistency, multi-turn handling, and bilingual parity beyond this accuracy split -- this comparison measures intent routing only. NOT VERIFIED: latency and deployability were reported by the agent that ran this (0.087ms vs 5.767ms median, 66x; 26ms vs 9,748ms cold start, 375x; a 1.8MB stdlib-only bundle vs a 1.9GB venv needing Python<=3.10) but were not re-measured identically inside this module, so they are reported as the agent's own finding rather than this module's. NOT VERIFIED: single seed, one training run -- no variance estimate exists for either system's score. NOT VERIFIED: the 14-probe OOS set is small enough that its confidence interval is wide even where the paired test is significant -- a held-out OOS set of 200-500 questions is the obvious next build, not done here. NOT CLAIMED that Rasa's own published benchmark numbers (ATIS/SNIPS/NLU-Benchmark, Bunk et al. arXiv 2004.09936) were reproduced -- those are different corpora; only Rasa's OOS recall (42.86%) is checked against that paper's own BERT oos-train figure (40.3%) as a sanity cross-check, and the two are close enough to corroborate rather than suggest a setup error.
